account.title: My account
account.pwHint: Other devices will be logged out after the change.
account.resetHint: Deletes all lessons and progress – you start again from 2 characters. Sound and speed settings stay.
account.logoutHint: Logging out deletes your data from this device (it stays on the server). Deleting the account irreversibly removes the account and all data on the server.
invite.title: Invite a new user
invite.linkHint: The link is valid for 7 days and only once. Send it to the invited person (e.g. by message):
users.title: Users
settings.languageHint: Applies to this device; when you are logged in, also to your other devices.
settings.speedHint: Spacing (Farnsworth) is shortened only after the full set: after 2 sessions ≥ 90 % with a stable reaction by one step, up to 20/20 WPM. With persistently low accuracy it gets longer. A manual change applies – the coach then waits for new data.
settings.wpmWarn: Below 15 WPM characters stop sounding like a whole and tempt you to count dots. 20 WPM is recommended.
settings.lessonHint: 5–10 min recommended. After 30 min of continuous practice the coach suggests stopping, above 60 min a day it warns.
settings.sitesHint: The home and outside versions are two separate apps (each with its own login); lessons are synchronized through the account.
keyboard.label: Keyboard
home.nextChar: Next character: "{ch}" – it is added once you have {acc} % in the last {n} characters of a lesson and recognise the newest character reliably and fast. From the 5th character on, progress is confirmed in the next session (at least 3 h later).
home.allChars: You have all characters of the set!
home.lessonInfo: {min} min · character {wpm} WPM · spacing {fwpm} WPM · tone {freq} Hz
home.speedProposal: The coach suggests a pace of {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM. {why} (Change it in Settings.)
home.loadDayWarn: Already {min} min today. Above {max} min a day little more is gained – better continue tomorrow.
home.loadSessionEnd: This session has lasted {min} min. I recommend stopping and continuing after a longer break.
home.loadFatigue: The last lesson showed fatigue – take a break of at least {min} min, the next session will then start with a warm-up.
home.copyDesc: Characters run as a stream without waiting – type as you go, even a character or a whole word later. Now: {name}, {gap}, {speed} WPM. Scoring aligns the whole line, the correction comes at its end.
home.copyWordLag: Goal of this step: a whole-word lag – type a word while the next one sounds; the ✓/✗ mark comes 2 words later.
home.copyMobile: On a phone I recommend typing each whole word only after it has finished.
audio.failed: Could not turn the sound on.
audio.failedResume: Could not turn the sound on – try Continue again.
intro.remember: Remember the sound. You can play it again.
discrim.question: Can you recognise the new character among similar ones?
lesson.fluency: Fluency block: known characters faster ({wpm}/{fwpm} WPM). Not counted in the result.
lesson.warmup: Warm-up – known characters first, to see what you remember.
lesson.rewarm: Warm-up after the break – known characters only for a while.
fatigue.whyTtr: For over a minute your reaction has been {pct} % slower than at the start of the session.
fatigue.whyAcc: For over a minute your accuracy has been {pp} points lower than at the start of the session.
fatigue.advice: That is usually fatigue – a short break (3–5 min: stand up, stretch, have a drink) usually helps more than more drill.
pause.rewarm: After the break you start with {s} s of warm-up with known characters.
pause.hint: Lesson time is stopped. After a break of at least {min} min the lesson starts with a short warm-up.
fatigue.noteEvent: Fatigue showed during the lesson ({what} than at the start of the session). Take a longer break before the next lesson – at least {min} min, or continue tomorrow.
fatigue.noteEndTtr: Towards the end of the lesson your reaction slowed down compared with the start of the session – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
fatigue.noteEndAcc: Towards the end of the lesson your accuracy dropped compared with the start of the session – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
fatigue.noteThirdTtr: Towards the end of the lesson your reaction slowed down by {pct} % – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
fatigue.noteThirdAcc: Towards the end of the lesson your accuracy dropped by {pp} points – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
verdict.confirm: Excellent, {pct} %! The character "{ch}" will be confirmed in the next session (in {h} h or tomorrow) – memory consolidates it over a break and sleep. Then the next character is added.
verdict.advance: Excellent! {pct} % in the last {n} characters. The next lesson adds the character "{ch}".
verdict.full: Excellent! {pct} % – you have the whole set.
verdict.few: Adding a character needs at least {n} characters in a lesson (now {trials}).
verdict.acc: Adding a character needs {need} % in the last {n} characters (now {pct} %). Continue with the same set – a plateau is normal.
verdict.ttrUnstable: {pct} % overall, but your reaction slowed down towards the end ({slower} %). The character is added once the reaction is stable – try again after a break.
verdict.newFew: {pct} % overall, but the new character "{ch}" sounded only {n}× ({need}× needed). Try a longer lesson.
verdict.newAcc: {pct} % overall, but the new character "{ch}" only {acc} % ({need} % needed). Practise it some more.
verdict.newSlow: {pct} % overall, but you react more slowly to the new character "{ch}" ({ttr} ms, others {others} ms). Practise it some more so that you recognise it instantly.
result.gapEase: Part of the lesson ran with longer gaps (accuracy dropped below 75 %) – that is fine, the coach gives you more time to recognise characters.
result.fluency: Fluency block: {pct} % at {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM (not counted in the result).
result.fluencyTtr: Fluency block: {pct} % at {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM, reaction {ttr} ms (not counted in the result).
result.warmupDrop: – a slight drop after a break is normal, it is not a regression; it evens out during the lesson.
result.warmupOk: – that is how well you remember the characters.
result.loadDayWarn: Already {min} min today. More than {max} min a day adds little – better continue tomorrow.
result.loadSessionEnd: The session has lasted {min} min – after {max} min concentration drops. I suggest stopping; what you learned consolidates over a break and sleep.
result.loadSession: Session {min} min. Take at least a 30 s break before the next block.
diag.latencyNone: – (turn the sound on with a Play button)

api.tooMany: Too many requests, wait a moment.

account.resetConfirm: Really reset the training? All lessons and progress on all devices will be deleted and you start from 2 characters.
account.resetDone: Training reset – you start again from 2 characters.
users.resetLinkConfirm: Create a new-password link for {nick}? It is valid for 3 days, only once; the training stays.
users.resetLinkHint: The new-password link for {nick} is valid for 3 days and only once. Send it only to them:

pw.tip: Tip: two words, a number and a symbol, e.g. Morning4!Coffee (but do not use this one). Do not use the password anywhere else.
quiz.intro: The answers only serve to set up the plan. They are not stored – only the result is (plan type and preferences). You can fill it in again at any time.
plan.pref.toneCheck: try the tone and volume in Settings, ideally with headphones
plan.pref.slowAnswer: there is plenty of time to answer, do not hurry
plan.fullSet: You have the whole character set. Now the goal is that every character stays ≥ 90 % and the reaction is fast.

plan.estimateLine.one: with {day} min of practice a day · {n} character left · {lo}–{hi} min per character
plan.estimateLine.other: with {day} min of practice a day · {n} characters left · {lo}–{hi} min per character

plan.fromData.one: Estimate from your lessons ({n} character added
plan.fromData.other: Estimate from your lessons ({n} characters added

plan.fromDataEnd: ). Later characters tend to be slower, hence the range.
plan.fromPrior: So far only an estimate by plan type. After the first 2–3 lessons the coach refines it by how fast you learn (people differ in speed up to 6×, but everyone reaches the goal).
plan.fluency: At the end of the lesson a {s} s fluency block.
plan.copyKeep: Character lessons keep serving for maintenance and warm-up.
plan.quizIntro: A short questionnaire (about 12 questions, 2 minutes) sets the lesson length and pace for you. After the first lessons the coach refines the plan by how fast you learn.
plan.entryTest: Returning operator: an entry test of all characters comes in a later version. For now you can set the number of characters manually in Settings.
dash.title: Progress and regularity
dash.empty: The overview appears after the first synchronization with the server.
dash.legend: Darker = more minutes; full colour = daily goal reached ({target} min).

dash.fatigue14.one: In the last 14 days fatigue showed in {n} lesson. Shorter blocks with breaks and training when rested help.
dash.fatigue14.other: In the last 14 days fatigue showed in {n} lessons. Shorter blocks with breaks and training when rested help.

dash.accNote: The coach keeps the lesson accuracy around 85 %, so do not expect a steady rise here – progress shows in characters and reaction.
dash.ttrNote: ms from the end of the character to the key press – lower is better. After a character is added it usually rises for a while.
dash.warmTip: warm-up {warm}, end of the previous session {prev}
dash.warmNote: Accuracy in the first 90 s of a session – the best measure of what you remember over a break and sleep.
dash.copyAccNote: Copy-behind lessons. The ladder step goes up after 2 sessions ≥ 90 %, after 2 sessions below 75 % it gets easier.
dash.lagNote: How many characters behind the sender you type. A longer and stable lag is the goal – your head holds more characters, in U4 whole words.
stats.title: Koch path
stats.intro: From the last {n} lessons. Learned {level} of {of} characters. Colour = accuracy, number = median reaction. Tap a character for details.
stats.empty: No data yet – statistics appear after the first lesson is sent.
stats.nextHint: This character is added once you meet the conditions for advancing.
stats.noConf: You have not confused "{ch}" with anything.
copy.phaseWordLag: feel free to type a whole word later
copy.listen: Listen and type – do not wait for the end.
copy.fatAcc: Accuracy in the last lines is {pp} points lower than at the start of the lesson.
copy.fatMiss: In the last lines {pp} points more characters are missing than at the start – the stream is running away.
copy.fatAdvice: That is usually fatigue – a short break (3–5 min: stand up, stretch, have a drink) usually helps more than more lines.
copy.legend: Sent on top, typed below. Green correct, red underlined a confusion, orange "_" missing, struck through extra.
copy.verdictMid: {acc} after alignment – a good range for learning. The next step comes from 90 % in 2 sessions.
copy.verdictLow: {acc} after alignment. Copying behind is a new skill – it is fine to type a word only after it has finished. After two sessions below 75 % the coach makes the step easier.
copy.lagDetail: Lag: median {lag} ch. ({ms} ms after the end of the character), 90 % of characters within {p90} ch., at most {max} ch.
copy.fatNote: During the lesson the coach suggested a break because of possible fatigue.
copy.drift: Towards the end of the lesson the lag grew by {n} ch. – try to type as you go so that the stream does not run away.
copy.counts: Correct {ok}, confusions {sub}, missing {del}, extra {ins} (of {n} sent characters, {rounds} lines).
copy.loadSessionEnd: The session has lasted {min} min – after {max} min concentration drops. I suggest stopping.
about.title: About
about.intro: A free Morse code receiving trainer. Author: OK2MTW.
about.licence: The app is free software under the licence EUPL-1.2 (European Union). You may use, study, modify and distribute it free of charge. If you make a modified version available to other people (even just over a network), you must make its source code available under the same licence.
about.morsePro: © Stephen C. Phillips – text to Morse conversion and timing (WPM, Farnsworth). EUPL-1.2. github.com/scp93ch/morse-pro, author of the website morsecode.world.
about.methodText: The Koch method (Ludwig Koch, 1936) and the character order of LCWO.net (Fabian Kurz, DJ5CW); Farnsworth timing; instant character recognition (ICR) training after morsecode.world and CWops CW Academy; findings on differences between learners (Long Island CW Club). We do not take over texts and content of these projects – only principles.
demo.title: Try it – three characters
demo.text: A short beginner lesson with the characters K, M and U, about a minute. You hear a character and answer by tapping the keyboard below (on a PC also with the keyboard). Nothing is saved.
demo.sound: Turn the sound on; headphones are best.
demo.noAudio: Sound could not be started – try again.
demo.listen: This is how this character sounds ({i}/{n})
demo.noAnswers: No answers – never mind, try again.
demo.reaction: Typical reaction {ms} ms after the end of the character
demo.more: In real training the coach adds characters one by one, adjusts the pace and watches for fatigue, and your progress is saved. Accounts are created by invitation only.
